seo.title: The MCP server — OpenMixer
seo.description: An MCP server over stdio that lets a coding agent read and write a running console through the console’s own contract, and read the contracts its DSP stages declare.

install.stdio: stdio; an MCP client starts it and speaks to it over the pipe.

hero.title: A console an agent can read and write through the contract every other client uses.
hero.lede: OpenMixer ships an MCP server over stdio. Its tools read and write a running console through the console’s own REST contract, and read the contracts each channel stage declares at the moment they are asked. It decides nothing: every answer is data the desk or the tree already holds, named with where it came from.

s1.title: Running it.
s1.p1: omx-mcp speaks MCP over stdio: an MCP client starts the process and talks to it over the pipe. There is no port, no daemon and nothing to leave running.

s2.title: {count} tools, in two families.
s2.p1: One family is the REST entity door as it stands: the roster, a row, its declared travels, one frame of a metered row, and a write. The other reads the contracts a channel’s DSP stages declare: the laws, the parameters and their limits. The table below is generated from the package’s registered tool table, not written by hand, and the package’s own test refuses a description that has drifted from the registry.

s3.title: One tool writes, and it writes once.
s3.p1: Every tool but one reads. console_patch sends a real write to a real desk, so it sends exactly one request, never retries it, and hands back the console’s status, its Allow header and its body as they arrived. A refusal is the desk’s ruling and is returned verbatim rather than interpreted, which is the same contract every other client works under: the console decides, and what comes back is what it decided.
s3.p2: The tool holds nothing back on its own account. A write that fires an operation the console’s own confirms sheet gates — a channel-config apply that would move gain, trim or pan is the example — is sent, and the console refuses it with CONFIRM_REQUIRED while the preview lists moves and the operator’s sign-off is on. The refusal comes back with the preview in the body, like any other answer. Calling again with confirm: true — which rides the delta as the row’s own confirm argument — applies it, because the agent has now been shown what it is agreeing to. The gate is the desk’s, so an agent, a browser and an OSC surface are refused identically and answer identically; there is no client-side policy to keep in step.
s3.p3: The metered row is the one place a read is not simply a GET. A pump-fed row measures only while something is watching it, so an unmeasured frame is followed by a single watch that closes the moment the first measured frame lands. No stream is left open.
s3.p4: The tools stand on a fake console with the real console’s shapes, checked across the wire on values rather than on shapes — a −20 dBFS reading has to decode to −20. A live desk is not part of that suite.
